title: End of Season and Closure of a Granite Ridge Season Pass Record
content:
Every pass record reaches the end of the season it was sold for.

**Expiry.** On the season's last operating day the pass stops admitting the holder and the record is marked expired, whether it was scanning freely or standing suspended. A pass carried forward that was never used in the season it was carried to expires in the same way.

**What expiry does not do.** Expiry does not cancel what is still owed: the instalment schedule runs to its end after expiry, and resort credit on the record keeps its own validity period.

**Closure.** A pass record is closed only when the pass account shows nothing left to collect and no credit left to spend. Both figures are read from the pass account itself.

**The last write.** Closure is the last write on the record and nothing is added to it afterwards.

**The price lock.** Where the tier carries next season's price lock, holding the pass to expiry entitles the passholder to the same price for the following season, claimed by opening a fresh pass record for that season rather than by reopening this one.

### Two hypothetical records at the season's close

*A Granite Ridge Summit Plus Pass standing suspended on the last operating day.* It is marked expired like any other record. Its remaining instalments continue to be presented after expiry, and the record is not closed until nothing is left to collect and no credit is left to spend.

*A Granite Ridge Local Pass with 40.00 of resort credit standing on the last operating day.* It is marked expired, but it is not closed while that credit stands; the credit keeps its own validity period, which on that tier runs 270 calendar days from the day it was issued.
